newsitem.title: USA: Mo. lawmakers okay $332 mln of tax cuts, credit.
newsitem.headline: Mo. lawmakers okay $332 mln of tax cuts, credit.

text.p: Missouri lawmakers have approved $332 million of tax cuts and credits, including elimination of the state's general food sales tax, a spokesman for Gov. Mel Carnahan said Monday.

Legislators voted on Friday to cut all 3 percent from the state contribution to the general sales tax on food totalling about $230 million as well as adding tax deductions for private pensioners and certain charitable contributions, Chris Sifford said.
Local sales taxes on food, which vary throughout Missouri, are not affected by the legislation, which Carnahan supports, Sifford said.
The elimination of the state general food sales tax also applies to vending machines and the sale of medical oxygen, he added.
The governor had made the food sales tax elimination a priority, but also agrees with the additions from the legislature, Sifford said.

The private pension deductions will be phased in over five years under the bill advanced to Carnahan. Donations to maternity, home and domestic violence programs will also be tax-deductible under the bill.
Missouri legislators adjourned a regular session shortly after passing the tax and reconvened Friday night to begin a special session to break a budget stalemate.
Lawmakers reached an impasse in their budget plans when they could not agree on state funding contributions to Planned Parenthood.
Both the house and senate introduced a number of bills on Friday night and the house budget committee has scheduled a meeting for Monday afternoon, Sifford said.
